correctness.rationale: Exact functional calculus uses the complementary projectors Π and I−Π. All offdiagonals equal (1−r)π_j and the minimum diagonal equals π_*+(1−π_*)r; the signed row absolute sum yields the infinity-norm formula. The gamma integral proves P_m(−z)>0 for even m and a unique zero plus stiff sign for odd m, while coefficient parity gives |r|<1. A single binary squaring yields multiplier r(z/2)^2∈[0,1), hence strict positivity for all admitted parameters. The [3/3] rational derivative has numerator (z²−15)²+375>0, proving one unique cutoff, its cubic and monotone n-limits. Replayed exact checker on 681 symbolic/matrix identities. Universal results are analytic; finite checking alone is not the proof.

originality.rationale: The claimed new mathematical object is the complete all-degree, arbitrary-stationary-law Markov positivity classification on rank-one reset generators, the sharp signed-mass norm, a uniform one-squaring repair, and a sharp [3/3] boundary. Earlier published work covers scalar Padé identities, Gauss/RK positivity theory, and particular Padé degrees. Primary full-text checks of Horváth (1998 Theorems 4–6 and 2005 Theorem 8/invariant-cone sections) treat broad classes with worst-case step thresholds rather than this exact reset-chain sign/norm law; no implication of the full combined statement was identified. This is a best-knowledge finding, not a uniqueness or publication-priority certificate.
residual_risks: The Horváth papers (1998, 2005) were obtained in full; selected relevant sections/theorems were read, but it is possible a specialized consequence is implicit in unexamined details or subsequent literature.
Only published scientific summaries rather than complete papers were inspected for two more recent special-case Markov positivity records.
Scalar parity facts and the first-order balanced-two-state exception are established prior ingredients; priority of the combined exact all-degree classification is not independently certified.
No literature search, even with primary text comparison, proves worldwide mathematical novelty.

value.rationale: Continuous-time reset chains are natural irreducible stochastic generators with tunable stationary imbalance; they isolate the distinction between algebraic group/stability preservation and entrywise positivity of a computational matrix exponential. The all-degree parity classification and necessary/sufficient minimal count of one binary squaring give a sharp nontrivial positivity benchmark for exponential integrators. The exact signed-mass amplification shows dimension-dependent spurious negative transition mass; the [3/3] cubic gives a usable sharp step selection rather than merely a sign example. It is not an arbitrary parameter slice, and it does not promise a general positivity guarantee beyond reset chains.
